sources.note: Nothing on Manta phonology at all: Manta [ALCAM 804] appears only twice, on p.3, in the ALCAM/Ethnologue classification lists. The report is a 1990 rapid-appraisal / RTT / lexicostatistics survey of Ipulo-Eman-Caka (Assumbo) and Icheve (Oliti and Bacheve; Mesaka) in Akwaya Subdivision; it has no phonology section and reproduces no wordlists (appendices are the ALCAM map, interview forms and questionnaires). Its single prosodic remark (p.33) is that Oliti speakers reported Bacheve pronunciation differing 'in vowel and tone quality' -- about Icheve, not Manta. No statement on stress or accent f…

sources.citation: Glottolog 5.1 languoid mant1267 and local CLDF sources.bib (hh.bib) a full-text search for stress/accent Manta [myg].
sources.note: Bibliographic only: descriptive refs are Ayotte & Ayotte 2002 and Blench 2010; Manta also appears as an ALCAM-derived wordlist in Piron 1996/1997 and as Nigerian 'Anca' [acb] in Blench 1999 (Ogmios 11). Uhle 1931 and Najlis 1978 are Ecuadorian 'Manta' mis-assignments.
Nothing; 'No reported resources in this language', no scripture or orthography work (hence no orthography statement to consult).

Typological tables take Manta as the Southwest Grassfields ('Western Momo') representative: vowels 7 oral / 7 nasal (source 'SIL wordlists'), tones 'H, M, L' (source 'SIL Wordlists'), word order 'No data'. Confirms that as of 2024 nothing beyond survey wordlists exists.
